Investors are increasingly scrutinizing manufacturing strategies, scalability and cost of goods long before commercialization, as CMC setbacks and production challenges reshape funding decisions across cell and gene therapy.
Start with the end in mind.
That is the message CDMOs, service providers and biotechs in the cell and gene therapies (CGT) space shared as the right manufacturing strategy to garner investment.
At Jefferies and Cell and Gene Therapy Live, an ancillary event to London Life Sciences Week, a venture capitalist and companies spoke to BioSpace about how, in the past five years, investors have increasingly focused on the later-stage manufacturing process involved in CGT, rather than the science alone.
The responsibility falls on biotechs to ensure they can detail the how and why of a long-term manufacturing plan.
“As investors deep in the cell and gene ecosystem, manufacturing capability has always been important,” said Sven Kili, partner at Saisei Ventures. “The change is now rather than just asking, ‘Can it be manufactured in Good Manufacturing Practice’, it’s asking, ‘Can it be scaled: how much and how cost effectively?’”
Increased CMC focus
That investors are concentrating on manufacturing capabilities is unsurprising. Manufacturing, Chemistry Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) and facility inspection deficiencies have become a leading cause of FDA Complete Response Letters (CRLs) for CGT programs.
CRLs are time consuming and expensive to rectify, particularly when a company is gearing up for commercial launch, said Stuart Lowe, head of advanced therapies at technology and product development consultancy TTP. Investors seek to mitigate this risk by insisting on derisked manufacturing strategy before first-in-human studies, he added.
In addition, with any new manufacturing process or equipment they want to see regulatory alignment and comparability data, he said.
Investors want a manufacturing story
The old-school biotech financial playbook of investing in good science alone isn’t as relevant for CGT, said Jason Foster, CEO and executive director at CGT CDMO Oribiotech. Considering how CGTs are inherently complicated due to their manufacturing requirements, investors have now homed in on the cost of goods (COGs) and throughput as CGT advances towards scale-up and market readiness.
Manufacturing scalability is now a key pillar alongside safety and efficacy, Lowe added. Despite billions of dollars invested in the field, only about 50,000 patients worldwide have received commercial CAR-T therapy since the first approval in 2017. The industry has not scaled manufacturing fast enough in the past five years.
Biotechs can’t assume that Big Pharma will take on the manufacturing risks they may have previously, Foster added. The smaller players face pressure to understand associated complexities they may have not had to before.
The onus is on biotechs to describe to investors a detailed manufacturing process and why it has been selected, said Bruce Culleton, CEO of ProKidney, which is developing an autologous cell therapy specifically for people with advanced chronic kidney disease. In addition, in terms of scale-up, the tech transfer process to a CDMO must be well-described, he added.
Kili agreed, adding as early-stage investors, a scale-up process cannot be mandated. But a rational and reasonable path to GMP and scale-up aligned with market assessment is desirable.
Backing management and execution
In terms of investment, Kili noted for company creation, Saisei Ventures ensures the manufacturability and scalability are prioritized with the science. Even for a seed investment, manufacturing consideration is expected. He added the firm also considers whether a company has the staff, in-house or consultants, to effectively manage any CDMO work, from a quality, speed, cost and timeline perspective.
“Just as I would like to see a product manager managing the path from translation to clinical development, the same applies to the CMC journey,” he added.
Lowe agreed, adding a biotech doesn’t need to have a commercial-ready platform at day one. But it needs to demonstrate that the ultimate manufacturing process is derisked to reach the desired scale. This can mean reviewing where investment in automation, process closure, personnel and facility specs is warranted, Lowe added.
COGs projections are hence a key metric for investors, Lowe said. But COGs can be influenced by manufacturing strategy decisions taken at the preclinical stage.
Without careful thought around how much to invest and where to invest in automation, companies may bake in a labor and facility intensive process that won’t be commercially viable, he added. Or they may overinvest in automation far beyond what the indication needs, meaning investment will take too long to pay back.

Tiny Cargo Trailer Turned 4-Season Off-Grid Mobile Home Is the Build You Have to See
26 photos
Photo: YouTube/Jacob Wagler
After years of reading about DIY van and bus conversions, the odd cargo trailer built, and countless other improvised solutions that aim to turn a life on the road into a comfortable, self-sufficient ones, you probably feel like you have seen it all already. This build will prove you you haven't.
Cargo trailer conversions are rarer than van or bus conversions, but they're still a popular choice among DIY (do it yourself) modern nomads.
Even in those cases in which they offer a smaller footprint than the other options, cargo trailers have the advantage of being extra stealthy, which is always a plus when you're forced to pull over on the side of the road in the city, extra sturdy, and easier to work with since they offer a neat blank page you can paint your ideal mobile home on.
They also require a bit more skill for the DIY-er, but skill is definitely not something that Jacob Wagler is short on. Wagler is a Canadian photographer and filmmaker that creates content solely on topics of photography. One of his most recent uploads is the exception, and it's also one of interest to us: his cargo trailer conversion that he called home for an extended period.
Photo: YouTube/Jacob Wagler Wagler is looking to sell his unit, so the video doubles as a sort of modern-day promo for it. For vanlife enthusiasts, it can serve as inspiration or even a model for a future build, especially since Wagler claims that his is the only conversion online with such a modular layout.
He's not exaggerating, either. This mobile home has perhaps the most creative and functional layout you're likely to ever come across in a cargo trailer conversion, and the fact that it's self-sufficient only adds to the appeal. It also packs a surprising amount of storage solutions, which is a true must-have for full-time living, and it's made to remain comfortable even in -30°C/-22°F temperatures.
Wagler started out with a 16-foot (4.9-meter) long tandem-axle V-nose trailer from Southland, with a standard double door on the back and a side entry. The home he's selling today is actually vastly different from the one he lived in a while back, for the simple reason that it's the second build on top of the same trailer.
Photo: YouTube/Jacob Wagler As the saying goes, second time's the charm, and it definitely applies to this conversion . After living inside the initial build for some time, Wagler decided to redo it, reconfiguring the interior, and changing things so that it would be more efficient in every way.
The result is a mobile home built with modularity in mind, with a full queen bed, a lounge area that you can't even see when you don't need it, a nice galley kitchen, and an even nicer, if wet, bathroom. It has storage aplenty, it has space to get work done, and it has self-sufficiency, while proving most of the creature comforts of home.
Wagler decided to put the bed on an elevated platform at the back and the bathroom at the front. The kitchen and workspace takes up the central part of the trailer, and whatever space is left can be used to entertain guests, rummage through the under-bed cabinets, and walk around without bumping into anything.
Photo: YouTube/Jacob Wagler The double doors at the back reveal the rear garage space, with container boxes secured in place by mesh netting. Wagler argues that plastic containers for everything are a neater, more organized solution for storage, as opposed to just having the items stacked away. They also help with the modularity of the build, allowing him to move them around easily by hand.
Also at the back, in a separate compartment, Wagler has storage for an LF Bros diesel heater and a Ninja pressure cooker, thus preventing it from taking up valuable space in the kitchen.
The main entrance is on the side of the trailer, lockable with a Peaklock circular door lock on the outside and a pair of deadbolts from the inside.
Photo: YouTube/Jacob Wagler Wagler strove to make the interior as modular as possible, so many items have double or even triple functionality. For instance, one of the storage drawers under the bed, sat on lockable wheels so you can move it wherever you need it, is also a bench (that still lacks cushions) and a fold-out single bed for emergency overnight stays.
Another large cabinet is a downsized wardrobe with hanging space and more plastic organizers, but also a counter extension for the kitchen once you slide it to face the wall so your clothes don't get stained and you add a removable countertop that usually sits in the bathroom. The main block of the kitchen is also Wagler's home office and the home's backup battery system.
Speaking of working from home, wherever home might be parked on any given day, Wagler made sure his trailer would allow for it. In addition to the Bluetti backup battery system, comprised of an AC300 3000W inverter and an Nvidia B300 system, he added to the trailer Starlink and four 320W solar panels.
Photo: YouTube/Jacob Wagler When the kitchen is not serving as his mobile office , it can handle cooking for one, with a removable induction cooktop, a compact sink, and a 12V fridge and freezer box. Storage for kitchen essentials is divided between the actual kitchen space and the middle cabinet under the bed, which is also the largest one.
In terms of comfort, this conversion comes with a 9,000-BTU Senville AC unit with heat pump (which seems to be the only feature that's drawing some negative comments online since it's mounted directly on top of the trailer), a backup camera, an on-demand tankless water heater, a MaxxAir fan in the bathroom, and a Joolca portable separating toilet.
Wagler doesn't say anything about the size of the holding tanks, but he does mention that he's moved the drains close to the underbody, so that there was no more danger of clipping them as it happened on version 1 of the build.
Photo: YouTube/Jacob Wagler This cargo trailer conversion is now for sale , but there's no mention about pricing. Instead, Wagler invites interested parties to reach out by filling a form, saying that he will contact those who make serious inquiries.

Unofficial MINI BUDDYMAN Project Focuses on the Car's British Roots and Diminutive City Car Presence
9 photos
Photo: car.design.trends / Instagram
The British MINI automaker , part of the BMW Group, has been pretty busy lately – albeit mostly with limited edition models rather than outright novelties like fresh nameplates or new generations.
The company has presented the Japan-only 2027 MINI Countryman Nightfall Edition earlier this month with just 200 units in right-hand-drive configuration for the land of the Rising Sun. Over in Australia, in turn, they honored six decades of ‘Bathurst glory’ with the ultra-limited Lucky 13 special edition, while at home the MINI Countryman SE Midnight Edition was introduced as another not-so-cheap limited model.
Even America has something new – the 2027 MINI Countryman Untamed Edition is an adventure-focused, all-terrain-dedicated version starting from $45k. It may sound like much, but it’s $20k cheaper than the UK’s Countryman SE Midnight Edition! Yikes.
Quite obviously, MINI has evolved over the years from its roots as a single-model ultra-affordable and tiny city car into the persona of a premium British brand under the guidance of BMW. But what if they went up against Elon Musk and his Tesla dream of making only autonomous vehicles like the Cybercab?
Well, someone has thought about that – a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. More precisely, the good folks over at " car.design.trends " have recently focused our attention on a hypothetical proposal for a brand-new tiny MINI concept car thanks to JungHoon Choi – who goes by ‘hoon.sktch’ on social media.
Actually, this virtual artist is an Automotive Exterior Designer at Tata Motors UK, so he knows what they’re doing – although this is an independent, unofficial, hypothetical design project. According to his idea, he conceived the MINI BUDDYMAN as a travel companion inspired by the original Mini car.
He explains: “MINI is an iconic British automotive brand, renowned for its distinctive design heritage. Its use of Union Jack-inspired elements, particularly in its lighting and DRL designs, continues to express its strong British identity. Inspired by this heritage, this project reimagines MINI as an iconic British mobility solution: a shared car designed to help travelers explore the UK with freedom and convenience.”
Directly taking cues from the original Mini, which was a lot smaller than today’s MINI vehicles , the BUDDYMAN would be the company’s autonomous car-sharing service that picks up travelers at an airport, for example, and takes them to explore the UK. It has flat surfaces and round forms along with signature Mini and British design elements – and also lacks a steering wheel.
Instead, it has what look like recycled parts – the wheels, tires, and lower-body protections appear to share the same design style, and the car is also a zero-emission vehicle, of course. So, what do you think – would you let yourself be driven in something like this around the UK? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Car Design Trends (@car.design.trends)

New Sporty-Looking Terramar Is a Cupra on the Outside and an Audi Sport Beneath the Skin
11 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
The Cupra Terramar recently turned two, and by today’s standards, this would mean that the company would start preparing its mid-cycle refresh. After all, production started in September 2024 at the Gyor factory in Hungary.
But is this indeed what we are looking at when it comes to the prototype pictured above? Actually, that would be a no, because as mentioned in the title, this vehicle may be a Cupra on the outside, but it is actually an Audi Sport beneath the skin. Or, better said, under the hood, as this thing is understood to be none other than the VZ5 version of the sporty crossover.
What does this mean? Well, that it should feature a 2.5-liter turbocharged five-cylinder engine. The mill in question is none other than Audi Sport’s unit, which powers the current RS 3 and was also found on the demised RS Q3. And it is also the mill of choice when it comes to the Cupra Formentor VZ5 , which sits at the very top of the lineup.
In the latter model, the engine is good for 385 bhp (287 kW/390 ps) and 354 lb-ft (480 Nm) of torque. A seven-speed DSG transmission delivers the output and thrust to the all-wheel drive system. The model hits 62 mph (100 kph) in 4.2 seconds, and that’s a three-tenth of a second improvement over the RS Q3, whereas the top speed has been electronically limited to 155 mph or 250 kph.
Photo: SH Proshots Mind you, there is absolutely no reason to believe that the Cupra Terramar VZ5 won’t retain these exact numbers. After all, this model is a more practical version of the Formentor, whereas the former is more of a coupe crossover. As a result, a possible VZ5 variant definitely won’t step on the toes of the Formentor VZ5.
We should also note the fact that this isn’t the first time we’ve seen the upcoming model, as this actually marks our third encounter with it. And to be honest, nothing has changed when it comes to the exterior design, as everything looks the same, including the wheels. Nevertheless, given that it will be an important addition to the company’s lineup, we couldn’t ignore it. Not to mention that instead of the Nurburgring, it was now caught in action on public roads.
Nothing has been confirmed when it comes to the Cupra Terramar VZ5 , but we know plenty of things about it. What we don’t is when it will premiere, and for this, we will turn to the rumor mill, which speaks about a possible debut sometime in early 2027. That is also when the model is understood to touch down at dealers overseas. Do you fancy the 2.5L transformation of the compact crossover?

Suzuki Launches a New Burgman Street Scooter, The 125 Is New in More Ways Than One
14 photos
Photo: Suzuki
In the spring of 2026, Japanese bike maker Suzuki released the new version of the Burgman Street scooter. Initially presented for the Indian market, because that's where it is produced, it has since started rolling to other markets as well. In Europe, the first new Burgman to get here is the 125.
Taking advantage of the MCL show at the NEC in Birmingham this past weekend, Suzuki unleashed the scooter with a lot of new and upgraded fittings, from the frame and engine to the electronics package.
I'll start with the frame, because it is this thing that keeps the two-wheeler together. Designed to be 500 grams (a little over one pound) lighter than before, it is supposed to offer as much rigidity as possible in the small-capacity scooter sector – that would be an increase in rigidity of 25 percent compared to before.
Inside the frame, hidden from view, Suzuki installed its 124cc, air-cooled single-cylinder engine from the Suzuki Eco Performance (SEP) family, heavily upgraded as compared to the versions already in use on some seven million scooters, so that it can deliver more torque at low to mid-range speeds.
Japanese engineers installed new crankcases that, in a twist, increased the under-seat storage capacity, a new crankshaft, new cam profiles, and a new clutch. The engine's airbox is new as well, and it is accompanied by changes to the intake port, mounting angle of the fuel injector, and exhaust system.
All the upgrades made by Suzuki allow the 2027 Burgman Street 125 to develop around eight horsepower at 6,500rpm and a little over ten Nm of torque at 5,250 rpm. That may seem quite a small number, but it more than gets the job done on a design that tips the scales at 254 pounds (115 kg).
To do that, the powerplant draws fuel from a 1.5-gallon (5.5 liters) tank that is accessible without opening the seat. The engine's fuel consumption rating stands at 141 mpg (1.6 liters/100 km).
Riding on new wheels shod in Dunlop D307 tires (the rear one is removable for a tire change without having to take off the scooter's exhaust silencer), the 125 offers an under-seat storage area’s of 25.9 liters, large enough to hold a full-face helmet, and a keyless ignition feature.
Suzuki plans to offer the Burgman Street 125 in Europe in three color choices: Pearl Grace White, Metallic Matt Stellar Blue, and Metallic Matt Black. The two-wheeler is expected to reach dealerships later in December, with a sticker that reads £2,599 in the UK. That's around $3,415 at today's exchange rates.
The new two-wheeler is not available in the U.S., where, at the time of writing, Suzuki is only selling the 400 model, which is, more or less, three times more expensive than the 125: $9,049.

2027 GMC Sierra HD Drops a 555-HP New Duramax V8 Under Its Hood, It'll Set You Back At Least $68K
21 photos
Photo: GMC
American carmaker GMC is not one to come under the spotlight all that often, as for years now it has been content to copy, to different degrees, whatever parent company GM has up its sleeve for sister brand Chevrolet.
The same continues to be the case with the 2027 Sierra HD pickup truck, which mirrors many of the fittings and changes of the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado HD . Yet, as announced at the end of last week, there are some particularities of the model that finally make the brand worthy of a story of its own.
Before getting into what the changes are, it's important to note that the 2027 GMC Sierra HD is in no way visually different than the current version. Connoisseurs, however, will be able to instantly spot the new variant by the sound it makes in one of its versions.
The truck is offered by GMC in this new form with the good-old gasoline 6.6-liter V8, enhanced a bit to be able to develop 412 horsepower and 472 lb.-ft. of torque, with the latter number claimed to be best-in-class.
Photo: GMC The version that sounds different is the one that relies on a new diesel V8 to get going, a clean-sheet GM design. Part of the Duramax family, it displaces 8.3 liters and is rated at 555 hp (something, too, described as best in class) and 1,230 lb.-ft. of torque.
Both engine offerings for the 2027 GMC Sierra HD work in tandem with an Allison 10-speed transmission, and they are not the only mechanical changes made to the truck for the new model year.
GMC throws into the mix rack-and-pinion electric power steering, something that's not at all common in this segment. The new setup replaces the previous hydraulic-assisted hardware offered.
The braking system of the pickup truck has been enhanced as well, with the fitting of a revised eBoost braking system that's a premiere in this segment as well. The setup consists of larger 14.6-inch front rotors and four-piston front calipers.
Photo: GMC GMC tinkered with the drive modes of the pickup truck to suit various needs and demands, and there are three major ones on deck, all modifying the performance and behavior of the engine, steering, braking, and chassis systems.
The Tow/Haul mode remains on deck for the 2027 model year, changing engine mapping, shifting, exhaust brake, grade-braking, EPS assist, and eBoost so that heavy loads can be hauled with ease.
How heavy the loads, you ask? GMC rates the Sierra HD at up to 20,000 pounds of towing capacity in standard configuration, and almost double that, 38,000 pounds, when featuring a max trailering gooseneck setup.
The truck's Off-Road mode is on deck to tweak ABS, traction control, and stability control so that the wheel is allowed more slip on loose surfaces. Finally, there is a new Terrain Mode, something the Sierra never used before.
Photo: GM Terrain Mode is only available on the AT4X model (more on trim levels later in this story), and it translates into the automatic application of braking power when the driver lifts their foot off the accelerator in 4HI or 4LO. It's a feature that should allow one-pedal control on steep grades and technical obstacles.
As said, the exterior of the truck is in no way different from what it used to be, but people might get a sense of novelty inside, especially when it comes to the technology aspects of driving the thing.
With the dashboard dominated by two screens, a 13.4-inch one for the infotainment system and a 12.3-inch instrument cluster, the Sierra now throws in 14 camera views designed to help with hitching, lane changes, reversing, and trailer monitoring, among others. An in-vehicle trailering app and trailer tire pressure and temperature monitoring are also thrown into the mix.
I mentioned the trim levels for the Sierra HD, and here they are, six of them for both gasoline and diesel variants, and a seventh exclusive to the diesel model. The gas-powered track costs at least $57,495 in the entry-level Pro variant, and starts at $89,195 for the most gifted AT4X.
Photo: GM The diesel offering opens with the Pro as well, but this time the starting price is significantly higher, at $68,895. The top-of-the-range is no longer the AT4X, but the diesel-exclusive Denali Ultimate, which will set people back $99,395.

Japanese Air Taxis to Start Operating in Australia’s Gold Coast by 2028
7 photos
Photo: SkyDrive
Japan’s best-known eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing) maker has reached the second phase of a major Australian collaboration aimed at introducing regular air taxi service across the famous Gold Coast, which could happen as early as 2028.
SkyDrive, maker of the compact SD-05 passenger-carrying electric air taxi, derived from the even smaller SD-03, once considered the most compact eVTOL in the world, is taking big steps toward commercial operations in one of the most important Aussie cities. The second-largest city in Queensland, and one of the most popular coastal destinations for tourists from all over the world, the Gold Coast is a perfect launch pad for urban air taxi operations.
This is a large-scale project, given that SkyDrive has now established official partnerships with both a private-sector player and the local government. In other words, it’s not just about delivering a few aircraft, but working with authorities and the local industry to create an entire AAM (Advanced Air Mobility) ecosystem.
Earlier this summer, SkyDrive first signed a LOI (Letter of Intent) with aviation operator Gold Coast Helitours. That was followed by a MoU (memorandum of understanding) signed with the City of Gold Coast, this month.
If things go according to plan, the Japanese SD-05 could herald Australia’s first official air taxi operations, and the big deadline that everyone is looking toward is the 2032 Summer Olympics, already known as Brisbane 2032. Although Brisbane is the official host, many of the sporting events that year will extend to the Gold Coast and other locations, and that’s an excellent opportunity to already have an air taxi system in place.
That is why SkyDrive and its partners are hoping to launch commercial operations here as soon as 2028, which would give them enough time to have everything working smoothly by 2032. This includes fully operational vertiports at multiple locations, maintenance bases, and confirmed routes for air taxi transportation and tourism, connecting the City of Gold Coast with other important hubs in the region.
Things really took off for the Japanese eVTOL maker after the successful demonstration flights at Expo 2025 Osaka, in Japan. It is currently the only AAM company in Japan to have reached this far in terms of type certification with the Japan Civil Aviation Bureau (JCAB), and its market success counts confirmed orders for more than 450 aircraft.
A lot of this success has to do with Suzuki being a strategic partner and investor. Recently, SkyDrive has confirmed that it’s gearing up to kick off mass production at a Suzuki facility in Japan, and the Group has also been instrumental in introducing the SD-05 eVTOL on major international markets, like India and the US.
Earlier this month, Japan’s Finance Minister attended a SkyDrive flight demonstration and was impressed with how quiet the electric aircraft was, and how quickly it was able to change direction. The SD-05 is primarily built for short-distance urban flights of around 15 km (9 miles) at a top speed of 100 kph (62 mph).

Refreshed Mercedes-AMG S 63 Arrives in Fantasy World Sporting a Crimson Shade and Fresh Wheels
7 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The Mercedes-Benz S-Class has been around since 1954 in various installments, with the current iconic name adopted in 1972, starting with the W116 model. Now, seven generations later, the flagship sedan is more in tune with the three-pointed star DNA than ever before.
The S-Class has always debuted the company’s latest innovations, but on this occasion, it merely followed a trend. The current W223 iteration was launched in 2020 with a classic sedan style unlike the BMW 7 Series, which has a more exotic split-headlight persona. At the time, it featured the latest powertrains, cockpit infotainment system, and assistance features, of course.
The pinnacle of the series were the Mercedes-Benz S 680 Guard 4Matic for those seeking protection like heads of state, the Maybach S 680 for customers who only care about luxury , and the AMG S 63 S E Performance, a complicated name for those asking for performance in a plug-in hybrid format.
This year Mercedes announced the refresh of the S-Class and had about 50% of the car modified, according to the company, making it the most comprehensive facelift ever for the flagship sedan. It followed the E-Class in gaining a headlight-connected grille, plus it also has dual three-pointed LED stars in the headlights and, for the first time, an illuminated hood ornament.
Around the back, there are now three star-shaped LED elements on each side, and the complex update also reworked the entire cockpit with a new water-cooled supercomputer running on MB.OS, plus the newer pillar-to-pillar MBUX Superscreen. The powertrains were also updated, including a new V8 engine, but the S 63 model, although spied by our partners while testing, has been absent from the facelifted roster.
With its fate hanging in the balance, it seems that it needs all the help it can get. At the moment, automotive news outlets have reported it as discontinued along with its 791-hp plug-in-hybrid V8 powertrain, trimmed from the lineup by Mercedes along with other models, such as the EQE Sedan and Maybach EQS 680 SUV.
The other Mercedes-AMG models like the GLE 63 S and GLS 63 did gain a refresh for the 2027 model year with all the updated goodies from the likes of the S-Class, but for one reason or another, the S 63 is nowhere to be found. For example, Mercedes offers in the US the refreshed S-Class with S 500, 580, and 580 e PHEV options, but the range-topping model is only the Maybach S 580 and S 680 series.
Well, here’s a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators who abandoned the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to try and convince Mercedes that it needs a facelifted S 63: Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on the performance version, showcasing it in a ritzy crimson hue and with all the facelift goodies plus a couple of new aftermarket wheel options. Cool or not? View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)

Cunard Ship Queen Victoria Is Now More Glamorous Than Ever
9 photos
Photo: Cunard
Queen Victoria, one of the fabulous cruise ships inspired by the legendary ocean liners of the Golden Era, has just emerged from a comprehensive refit looking even more elegant, and also flaunting some new amenities.
Queen Victoria is one of the newer ships added to the Cunard fleet. Construction began in 2004 at the famous Fincantieri shipyard in Italy, and the ship was officially christened in December 2007 by the then Duchess of Cornwall, Camilla. Flaunting close to 1,000 feet of pure elegance, this modern classic ship can accommodate a little over 2,000 guests, catered to by a crew of 980.
In mid-October, Queen Victoria sailed to Rotterdam for a relatively quick, but comprehensive refurbishment at the prestigious Damen Shiprepair. Earlier this month, the beautiful ship has re-emerged from that refit looking more glamorous than ever and ready to enchant its guests with refreshed looks and trendy amenities, but without dimming its old-world charm.
Over the years, Queen Victoria has become famous for unique features, such as housing the Royal Court Theater, which is the first theater at sea to have West End-style theater boxes, one of the biggest libraries at sea, and a spectacular Grand Lobby with marble floors, a majestic staircase, and a dazzling chandelier. This Grand Lobby quickly became iconic and has now been at the center of this recent refit.
Completely different from the cookie-cutter cruise ships out there, all Cunard ships represent a sophisticated and thoughtful tribute to classic ocean liners (Queen Mary 2, in particular, is considered the only true ocean liner in the world right now), and this includes a certain aesthetic, and entertainment spaces such as theaters, libraries, and salons for the afternoon tea – all of which literally immerses guests into the glamorous world of the past.
Queen Victoria’s iconic three-story Grand Lobby is now truly royal, as the new aesthetic was directly inspired by the famous orange blossom jewelry gifted to Queen Victoria by Prince Albert. The floral borders of the Royal Palaces were also a source of inspiration, as well as butterflies, hinting at the Royal Family’s support for environmental initiatives.
New amenities onboard the refurbished ship include the Pavilion Wellness Café, first introduced on the Queen Anne and Queen Elizabeth ships. This trendy dining space offers plant-based menus and sustainably-sourced meat options. The Britannia Deluxe Oceanview is another novelty, this time as a brand-new premium suite category. As the name suggests, it features floor-to-ceiling windows for expansive views.
The newly glammed-up Queen Victoria is gearing up for a 109-night World Voyage, beginning on January 10, 2027, that will take guests to ports from Hong Kong and Sydney to Dakar and Senegal.
In the meantime, the legendary Queen Mary 2 is also preparing for a refurbishment at Damen Shiprepair Brest, in France. The ship is set to enter dry dock in the early spring of 2027, and the entire redesign will be led by one of Queen Mary 2’s original designers, Chris Finch.

As the FDA homes in on a unified rare disease strategy, Praxis Precision Medicines is anticipating its first approval with two near-term shots on goal—a treatment for a devastating rare seizure condition, followed by a drug for a more common neuro condition.
Biotech’s self-described “oddball” is nearing two major inflection points. With two FDA action dates between Christmas and the end of January, Praxis Precision Medicines’ wide-ranging pipeline is on the cusp of delivering its first medicines to the market.
Praxis’s R&D portfolio spans the neuro spectrum, with therapies in development for both ultrarare and more common central nervous system (CNS) diseases. “That might make us a little bit of an oddball out there, because sometimes companies focus in one side or the other,” CEO Marcio Souza told BioSpace .
Marcio Souza
Praxis Precision Medicines
The company’s first decision date falls into bucket number one. On or before Dec. 27, the FDA is expected to decide on relutrigine for SCN2A and SCN8A developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEE)—devastating conditions involving “unrelenting seizures,” according to Souza. Patients require 24-hour care and have a very high mortality risk, he said. “I personally believe it should be life-changing when you meet one of those patients.”
Praxis’ other upcoming FDA decision, for ulixacaltamide in essential tremor, is anticipated a month later, on or before Jan. 29, 2027. Essential tremor is the most common movement disorder in the U.S., Souza said, placing this indication squarely in Praxis’ second bucket.
The Boston-based biotech is also a bit of a renegade, pushing beyond the traditional CNS development playbook, the CEO said.
One of the biggest ways Praxis does this, he continued, is by asking how patients experience the disease “and then going back from there, having the courage to actually design the studies that . . . answer that question.”
While Souza noted that this approach is often “at odds” with established practices, it is quite in line with the FDA’s new Rare Disease Framework Initiative . Announced on October 15, the initiative lists as its second commitment “embedding the patient’s voice both early, and at clearly defined milestones, in the drug development and review process.”
Souza called the FDA’s new rare disease framework “fantastic,” adding that it has been “a very long time in the making.”
He added a word of caution: “I am not sure yet that there is the kind of alignment and the kind of momentum that is required for that [vision] to become a reality,” he said. “But I’m very optimistic about it—maybe [for] the very first time.”
FDA
FDA’s new rare disease framework aims to leverage patient voices for better innovation
Inclusion of the patient perspective is currently an “optional” part of the rare disease drug development process, CBER Director Karim Mikhail told BioSpace . Mikhail, along with his CDER counterpart Michael Davis and other agency rare disease leaders, is trying to change that.
November 9, 2026
·
7 min read
·
Heather McKenzie
Read more
Decision time
Relutrigine is an oral drug that blocks the persistent flow of current across sodium channels. When left unchecked, this inward flow of sodium ions is a key driver of seizures in patients with DEE. If approved, relutrigine will be Praxis’ first marketed drug.
In the Phase 2 EMBOLD study , 51 patients on relutrigine saw a 53% placebo-adjusted reduction in seizures over 16 weeks, Praxis reported in December 2025. Patients treated with Praxis’ drug also saw a 66% increase in motor seizure–free days. The results were so positive that a Data Monitoring Committee recommended the study be stopped early for efficacy.
Praxis had hoped for approval of the sodium channel blocker by Sept. 27, but the FDA classified additional sensitivity analyses of existing clinical data as a major amendment to the original application, delaying the verdict by three months. The agency did not request any additional trials, nor did it point out any safety or manufacturing concerns, Praxis said in a June 29 announcement , leading Jefferies to call the extension a “fairly benign delay.”
Neuroscience
Praxis Ends Epilepsy Study Early Due to Strong Results, Heads to FDA
Praxis Precision Medicines has also announced a “successful” pre-NDA meeting with the FDA for its essential tremor drug candidate ulixacaltamide, for which an approval application is slated for early 2026.
December 5, 2025
·
2 min read
·
Tristan Manalac
Read more
During an Investor Day update on Nov. 12, the biotech shared open-label extension (OLE) data from EMBOLD showing benefit through 18 months, with an 86% reduction in seizures from baseline. In a note following the event, Jefferies analysts said the new OLE data support relutrigine’s durable drug effects.
There has never been a drug developed for DEE, according to Souza.
A lot of companies “shy away from problems like this,” he said, adding that he gives “a lot of credit to the FDA for actually pushing us throughout the process.” Souza further credited leadership in the FDA’s Office of Neuroscience and its neurology divisions as “individuals that really care about patients.”
As for Praxis’ other product on the cusp of potential approval, the biotech shared an early analysis of the Phase 3 Essential3 long-term safety study in its Nov. 12 update. Patients with essential tremor who completed efficacy assessments after receiving ulixacaltamide for around 95 weeks showed durable and improving response over time on an activities of daily living (ADL) scale, “further supporting ulixacaltamide’s use as a chronic therapy,” according to the biotech’s press release.
Ulixacaltamide “seems likely to be FDA-approved” by the Jan. 29 PDUFA date, Jefferies said following the update.
In addition to the upcoming decision in essential tremor, Praxis plans to launch studies of ulixacaltamide in Parkinson’s disease, restless legs syndrome and autism spectrum disorder next year, according to the biotech’s recent update.
Ulixacaltamide and relutrigine are both based on Praxis’ Cerebrum small molecule platform. Meanwhile, elsunersen, in Phase 3 development for early onset SCN2A DEE, leads the company’s Solidus antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) platform. Elsunersen, which selectively decreases SCN2A gene expression to treat seizures in patients with gain-of-function SCN2A mutations, received FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation in June.
Jefferies isn’t the only analyst firm bullish on Praxis.
“The Investor Day reinforced our confidence in the near-term [essential tremor] opportunity while highlighting an increasingly compelling longer-term pipeline story,” Truist Securities wrote in a Nov. 13 note.
“[W]ith two potential near-term launches and a broadening pipeline behind them, we believe Praxis is increasingly positioned to emerge as a multi-product CNS company with several avenues for future growth and value creation.”

Chinese Air Taxi Completes Sri Lanka’s First Passenger-Carrying Autonomous eVTOL Flight
7 photos
Photo: EHang
EHang adds another international industry-first under its belt, as one of its pilotless aircraft carries out the first-ever passenger-carrying autonomous eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing) flight in Sri Lanka.
The passengers of this historic flight with no pilot onboard were Sri Lankan officials, Minister Karunathilaka and Deputy Minister Kodithuwakku. The EH216-S aircraft carried out this inaugural flight in Colombo, as part of a wider ceremony attended by numerous Sri Lankan and Chinese officials.
With this flight, Sri Lanka officially becomes the 24th country where the EHang EH216-S has completed flight demonstrations. For the Chinese company, it marks another significant milestone, as its first official flight in South Asia. Sri Lanka is a special partner for EHang, as the first country that has adopted the EHang Global Fast Track Program back in August 2026.
Through this program, the Chinese eVTOL maker actively works with national and local players in the private sector and authorities to establish an AAM (Advanced Air Mobility) ecosystem, including the regulatory framework, vertiports, air taxi routes, and other essential pillars for autonomous eVTOL operations.
In Sri Lanka, as well as the other countries who are part of the program, the EH216-S won’t be limited to air taxi service. While primarily geared toward aerial tourism, this pilotless electric aircraft can also be used in search-and-rescue missions, disaster relief, and critical logistics for hard-to-reach areas that are typically more isolated.
The EH216 has completed more than 100,000 safe flights to this date, with no pilot onboard. A newly-established strategic hub in Thailand will focus on EHang’s expansion in Southeast Asia, while Kazakhstan is at the center of its Central Asia strategy. Last year, the Chinese company confirmed plans to launch large-scale production in Kazakhstan, following a collaboration with Allur Group, a big automotive manufacturing company in the area.
The collaboration targets what could become the first-ever eVTOL assembly facility in Central Asia, with a production capacity of around 200 aircraft per year.
In 2025, EHang has also completed the first passenger-carrying autonomous eVTOL flight in Africa. It took place in Kigali, Rwanda, during the 9th Aviation Africa Summit and Exhibition, with support from China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC).
None of these pioneering flight demonstrations with passengers onboard would have been possible without one thing: the EH216-S was the first passenger autonomous eVTOL in the world to secure full certification. China's civil aviation authority was much faster than its international counterparts in establishing all the certification requirements and regulations, allowing EHang to also move much faster through the whole process.
The Chinese eVTOL maker now has all the certifications in hand to focus on global expansion, including the PC (Production Certificate) that allows it to mass-produce autonomous aircraft in the EH216 series (passenger and cargo).

Air Force Pumps $3.5M in Blended-Wing-Body Cargo Drone Made by Natilus
20 photos
Photo: Natilus
For several years now, an American aerospace company called Natilus has been trying to come up with a new way of designing aircraft. Ok, not entirely new, but never attempted on such a scale before. And that new way of designing an aircraft, blended-wing-body (BWB), just got a major boost thanks to official military backing.
The Natilus product the Air Force sees as potentially useful for its needs is called Kona, and it is a BWB in that it comes with no clear distinction between its main fuselage and its wings. By trade, it is an optionally piloted aircraft born to carry cargo.
The company chose to go down the path of a BWB design on account of the advantages it brings along compared to a conventional setup. That includes, among other things, more lifting power, less drag, and more interior space.
In the case of the Kona, as in the specific design being researched right now for the needs of the USAF, that translates into a 3.8-ton lifting capability and a maximum range of 920 miles (1,481 km).
These capabilities place the mildly strange-looking aircraft smack down between what a light utility aircraft the likes of the Cessna C-208 and a heavy-lift Lockheed C-130 Hercules can do. Moreover, the Kona also throws in the ability to take off and land from and on short fields and without a pilot on board.
On top of everything, it has been imagined in such a way as to be compatible with existing cargo infrastructure, and its fuel consumption needs should be some 30 percent lower than in the case of conventional aircraft of similar size.
I said earlier that the U.S. military is very interested in this design, and one only needs to look at the $3.5 million it pumped at the beginning of the month into research, development, test, and evaluation of the Kona .
The company plans to use the money to speed up work, aiming for full-scale flight testing and an operationally relevant U.S. Joint Force demonstration at a yet-undisclosed time in the future.
Initially, the company started work on the BWB with the civilian sector in mind, but, as with many other aerospace innovations, it has immediately attracted the eye of the military. That's because, aside from being able to carry cargo, it could be adapted to perform communications relay missions and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) flights.
There is no word yet on when the militarized Kona will be ready, but the company did reveal that it is now moving to Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Part 23 certification (normal category airplanes up to 19 seats) and full-scale flight testing. We'll keep an eye on things and report back when that (or some other) milestone is reached.
